title: Mark, Luke and Acts
summary: Three New Testament books join the library: Mark, Luke and Acts, each translated fresh from the Greek, with notes on the hardest passages, the manuscript differences (including Mark's endings and the longer and shorter texts of Luke and Acts), who each speech and parable was first for, and where the churches read them differently. Nineteen new topic pages follow the story from the ascension and Pentecost through Paul's journeys.

items.text: Added Mark: a Plain English translation of all 16 chapters, with 566 study notes and 127 manuscript differences explained.
Added Luke: a Plain English translation of all 24 chapters, with 1031 study notes and 177 manuscript differences explained.
Added Acts: a Plain English translation of all 28 chapters, with 909 study notes and 207 manuscript differences explained.
19 new topic pages, including The Acts of the Apostles, Sayings of Jesus Outside the Gospels, Apollos, The Ascension of Jesus and Corinth.
Notes across the Old Testament, Matthew, John, Revelation and the books outside the 66 that quote Mark, Luke or Acts now use their new translation.
The Elders topic page now covers the whole Bible: Israel's elders, the elders of the first churches and the twenty-four elders of Revelation.
